notes.title: Fog Visuals, Stability, Updated Demo, And Optimization
notes.content:
[h3]Fellow Mixonauts! I bring more stability and optimizations! [/h3][p]A lot has been going on over the last few months, life has been good but also busy! The goal of this update was to try and fix issues related to people freezing during load, crashing in certain spots, and in general improving performance. From my testing, the game should be around 15-30% faster to render and also be much nicer to lower end machines when setting everything to low. I am also excited that for the first time in a year or so I will now be focusing on features that will improve the audio production aspect of the game! Stay tuned and checkout everything below for more details on what's new and coming next![/p][previewyoutube="rljOwya8tSI;full"][/previewyoutube][h3]New Fog Visuals Comparison and Performance Results[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/15106be8118a4d2148275e95bbbb5058324023f8.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/b3d3f0785dbd8d16b32626f34df7561e9268739b.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Bug Splat integration allowing me to see crash reports![/h3][p]Filling in crash reports and sending them is incredibly valuable and helps me get an idea of how stable the game is![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/6b4ec118f4dc401407ed4de98a431ca8ba96f88d.png"][/img][/p][h3]Full List of Changes[/h3][list][*][p]Engine upgrade to Unreal 5.6 to take advantage of megalights. This will become more important in future updates. Currently the HQ is the only place that uses it.[/p][/*][*][p]Turned off Unreal Nanite (Wasn't worth the cost for how little the assets in Mix Universe use it)[/p][/*][*][p]Turned off Unreal Lumen (Might turn this back on later, visuals aren't any different)[/p][/*][*][p]Made a custom asteroid model to replace the nanite version that looked bad on lower end machines.[/p][/*][*][p]Upgraded the Voxel Landscape System to be much quicker to update and free from splits and chunk updates.[/p][/*][*][p]Added custom foliage generation system for the voxel landscape (Will be used later for generating other things for the game)[/p][/*][*][p]Added ability to change voxel landscape type per node. (This will be expanded upon in future content updates)[/p][/*][*][p]Updated foliage for landscape so that it scaled density based on foliage quality.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated Fog to be particle-based which is 50% cheaper to render than the previous fog solution. This also scales based on Visual FX quality so that there are less particles on lower end machines[/p][/*][*][p]Disabling view fog will also reset the fog simulation texture so that it doesn't leave artifacts behind.[/p][/*][*][p]Fog texture for clearing out fog around nodes will now scale based on settings and also not compute after a certain distance to the camera.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where modulator and radar node rings weren't using the right fog settings.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated Steamdeck graphics settings so they automatically get set unless you turn off the automatic settings. This ensures that players get the best gameplay/visuals/performance ratio out of the box.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix Crash/freeze when loading into mixes due to multiple calls of flush async loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix Crash caused when being rate limited by modio[/p][/*][*][p]Fix Issue where when offline, mod status was invalid[/p][/*][*][p]Fix Issue where when being rate limited from loading too many mixes, soft fail until the rate isn't limited anymore. (Somewhere around loading more than 60 images a minute causes rate limiting)[/p][/*][*][p]Fix memory leak related to not clearing loaded images from the galaxy map[/p][/*][*][p]Loading images in the galaxy map is now based on which mixes you can actually see.[/p][/*][*][p]Universe Mixes should load more reliably now and not be as easily rate limited as before.[/p][/*][*][p]Turned on GPU Simulation for all particle FX related to nodes and links, should be much cheaper on the CPU for rendering larger mixes.[/p][/*][/list][h3][/h3][h3]Also, the demo is now aligned with the current version of the game.[/h3][p]The demo version of Mix Universe was rather outdated and full of bugs that were fixed in the full game, but never ported back to the demo version. Now the demo is aligned with the current version of the game and hopefully will come along with the newer updates as well.[/p][list][*][p]Demo play area size is now bigger as requested by a few mixonauts.[/p][/*][*][p]Demo Universe is offline to prevent people from being able to mess with the universe mixes without the full game. [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]What's next?[/h2][h3]1. The Sample Library Update[/h3][p]This update will be a huge deal and try to cover a few things. No promises, but I am trying my best to hit all of these.[/p][list][*][p]Allowing Players to own 100% what they make in the game for commercial use and identifying samples in which do not allow this. (Certain drum samples fall into this category)[/p][/*][*][p]Controlling the attack, decay, sustain, and start time of a playing sample.[/p][/*][*][p]Some other cool ideas I'll talk about later.[/p][/*][/list][h3]2. The Modulation Update[/h3][p]The goal of this will be to allow automation of modulation elements. This I am hoping to pair up with movable nodes which I think will take mix creation to the next level and allow for things like filters to change much easier over time and more dynamically.[/p][h3]

The Universe[/h3][p]We now have 188 mixes in the universe! Seeing these over the past few months have really shown me how talented and creative the mixonaut community really is. I truly enjoy them at any complexity.

notes.title: The Universe Update
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=fRl1iXNt5tk;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Mix Universe has a universe![/h2]

This update initially was going to be more of a rework of the original steam workshop support, but given the limitations of steam workshop and not having the ability to expand to other platforms easily in the future, I took this opportunity to implement mod.io instead from the ground up (Also the workshop support I had currently was really hacky!). What this means is that sometime in the next 2 months, the steam workshop will be turned off completely in favor of mod.io.

[h2]Nothing is lost![/h2]
Everything you uploaded to the steam workshop already will be auto-downloaded and added to the list of mixes you can add to your galaxy allowing you to add them to the universe seamlessly in-game using mod.io. You also are not required to make a new account for mod.io, it will automatically do this using your steam account when accepting the privacy policy and EULA when entering the galaxy map.

In a nutshell, using mod.io instead of the steam workshop allows this.
[list]
[*] Easier to develop and maintain. (Steam requires you to play in standalone mode to test anything.. which is a HUGE pain for unreal dev)
[*] If / When Mix Universe goes to other platforms, the universe support will work with all content uploaded on all platforms! This is the biggest win.
[*] Overall speed and stability of mod.io when it comes to searching and downloading mixes is much better!
[/list]

For some credibility, mod.io is also used in Besiege, Space Engineers, and Baldurs Gate. I wish I would have known about it sooner!

Anyhow, I hope this is only a minor upset as you have to manually re-upload anything you had on the steam workshop before. I have also downloaded everything locally so if you for whatever reason have issues getting your mix off of the steam workshop, please ping me in discord or the contact form.

Ok here's what is new!!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/bbbcf92d8d363871d515288a52a1966289f35af5.png[/img]
[h2]The Galaxy and Universe Map[/h2]
[list]
[*] A complete "workshop" overhaul using mod.io now called the Universe in-game.
[*] 3 Different world modes right now. Map screen, Headquarters, and an opened Mix. All of which can be switched to seamlessly.
[*] The Galaxy map has 2 different galaxies, your galaxy where you can edit, open, upload, or move around your mixes to organize them and the explore galaxy which is more for when you are looking for mixes to gain inspiration from!
[*] The Universe map is where everyone's uploaded mixes will be displayed for everyone to see! After uploading, you can then place your mix anywhere in the universe!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/840c5699a44347ed9a105c43e816f03564cb7984.png[/img]
[h2]Cool art things[/h2]
[list]
[*] Completely streamlined transitions and visuals from going to HQ, Galaxy Map, and an opened Mix.
[*] Added collision and shadows to planets, drum rings, and other various meshes that are part of the batched particle FX system.
[/list]

[h2]Another Major Gamepad Pass[/h2]
Some players have given some great feedback on how terrible the gamepad support was before.  I’ve spent a lot of time trying to make the gamepad support is much better now so PLEASE once again tell me how much you hate or love it haha!
[list]
[*] By default, left stick now moves around instead of moving the cursor. 
[*] The cursor is only movable when you have something selected (To help click on UI’s) 
[*] You can use the D-Pad to navigate buttons quicker, but sometimes it might be hard to navigate to where you want it, instead the left stick cursor should help in those spots.
[*] I highly recommend re-playing the intro tutorial to learn the gamepad buttons or heavily check the bottom left corner when hovering over things.
[/list]

[h2]Other Fixes and Optimizations[/h2]
[list]
[*] All save data is now in your %LocalAppData%/MixUniverse folder INSTEAD of your documents. All data is copied upon first launch with the new update its up to you to delete the old data in your documents. This is a precautionary just in-case something goes wrong and you lose data during the copying process, but it should be rather stable and safe! This fixes issues with controlled folder access on windows not allowing people to save OR OneDrive not allowing Mix to edit documents. 
[*] Mixes are now 1/10th the size they were before and load 10 times faster!
[*] Backups and Auto saves for mixes now are stored per individual mix (Up to 10 at a time per mix) This way you can easily restore a backup or autosave without having to load into the mix, and save as.
[*] Fixed issues related to elements and sounds getting stuck and not playing anymore.
[*] Fixed first time loading issues where it would skip certain sounds.
[*] Fixed double click times not registering properly OR registering on objects you didn’t double click.
[*] Mix visuals are now limited by a certain amount of compute time in order to keep the audio and movement as smooth as possible. This results in less smooth audio synced visuals on mixes that are more intensive to your CPU.
[*] Added ability to start and stop a mix during flight mode and walking (Control or X + SpaceBar)
[*] Added a skip tutorial button in the pause menu when playing a tutorial.
[*] Added a pivot visual for the edit camera. The pivot will auto re-adjust if you get to close to it or if you stop rotating the camera. You can also hit F to re-focus the pivot at any point when something isn't selected.
[*] Added optional camera auto center on selection for both keyboard and mouse and gamepad separately. Can be useful for folks who don’t like navigating around with WASD as much.
[*] Updated icons for main UI buttons so they are easier to know what they are.
[*] like and that position will show for others.
[*] Removed ability to “save as” to reduce accidental overwriting of mixes you don’t have open.
[*] Intro tutorial now includes a section at the end that goes over how to use the galaxy map, create new mixes, and have fun. Now it blends into gameplay much better when it finishes.
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Achievements are completely borked. (Hopefully will fix this one soon!)
[*] Currently, I am hunting down a click issue where sometimes the first time you click something doesn't select it. Seems to be some order of when you click off of something else, but haven't been able to reproduce consistently yet.
[*] Editing the name of a mix after uploading can sometimes result in very long sync times until going to the HQ and back into the map screen.
[/list]

[h2]What is next?[/h2]
The next updates will be arguably the coolest in the game's development because the core of the game is starting to harden a bit. The last year or so I have been just grinding away at very very core implementations and features that don't really push any of the boundaries of the musical aspect of the game, but that's about to change!

Each of these bullet points I consider to be their own updates.
[list]
[*] Upgrading to UE5.5 for Megalights and Voxel Plugin 2.0. This should hopefully be the shortest interval between updates we've had so far!
[*] Modulation and First MetaProgression pass. I'll give more details on this later, but you can expect to see some cool updates along the way as I start upgrading and finalizing the different FX and other ways you can manipulate the sound being played. I have been daydreaming about doing this for the past 2 years so IT'S FINALLY TIME!
[*] Midi import/export support
[/list]

Keep an eye on the roadmap on main page for more. As always thank you so much for your support so far and please join the discord

notes.title: The Core Gameplay Update is out now!
notes.content:
Hello folks! Here we are in august and finally I have great news. Mix Universe now has a free demo, in-game tutorials, the ability to walk, run, jump, activating rings when you hit them, and much more!

If you are wondering why it took so long. Here's a video going over what happened month-to-month along with a showcase mix at the end.

[previewyoutube=iVwHONanlS0;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/9b77b230274a71b3a6ec260cc62cff4f22174545.jpg[/img]

[h1]Full Release Notes[/h1]

[h2] New Stuff [/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]New In-Game Tutorials - 6 of them to start. [/b]More coming later! Lots to learn which will hopefully help make it easier to make mixes for a lot of folks!
[*] [b]New Contextual Hint Display[/b] - now in the lower left it will try and tell you what buttons to press during certain interactions. This needs to be filled out a bit more, but is very helpful on controller. Can toggle it off in gameplay settings.
[*] [b]New Activator Ring Nodes[/b] - Considered experimental, but rather playable still. New demo mix in the included mixes has them setup in a fun way (In the video above)
[*] [b]New Layer edit panel.[/b] Entirely refactored and allows up to 32 layers now.
[*] [b]New Community tab[/b] for mixes which show the latest 50 uploaded mixes to the workshop.
[*] [b]New Ability to walk, run, and jump[/b] (Double jump to go back into flight mode!)
[*] [b]New Animations in flight mode when boosting[/b]
[*] [b] New Painting nodes by clicking and dragging during placement[/b]
[*] Workshop mixes notify the discord server when uploading to public to help visibility and notify people who might be interested in seeing what's new!
[*] [b]New Beach environment![/b]
[*] [b]New when starting a new mix, there will be an auto-generated one to play with instead of just a blank canvas.[/b] You can easily delete by clicking and dragging to select. 
[*] [b]New Headquarters[/b] for you to choose what to do next
[*] [b]New Added back a simple form of grid snapping.[/b]
[*] [b]New You can now load mixes from the headquarters.[/b]
[*] [b]New customize character color![/b] Will keep adding to this![/b]
[*] [b]New ability to make patterns by clicking and dragging links to nodes.[/b]
[*] [b]New volume control on a sound instead of having to use an FX element.[/b]
[/list]

[h2] Bug fixes and stability [/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed Steam input only working the first time for the steamdeck.
[*] Quite a few stability fixes with audio playback. Mixes shouldn't skip nodes or have delayed audio on nodes now.
[*] Improved performance of audio playback. Should be able to handle more nodes.
[*] Improved performance of gathering nodes which is used by modulators, radar nodes, and certain visualizers.
[*] Fixed Voxel Memory for landmass nodes when placing lots of them. Should max out at around 1gb of added memory now instead of 8-12gb
[*] Fixed issues when moving nodes around for height detection. Now it will never go lower than the node's original starting height position but will go higher if moving over landmasses.
[*] Fixed Activators sometimes not playing when set looping value to 1.
[*] Fixed many issues with gamepad where input could get stuck or un-usable. Should be mostly stable now. There might be a few interactions with dragging elements that will get stuck on hover, but nothing that has been consistently reproable yet.
[*] Fixed default performance settings so that it can be more compatible with more machines. 
[*] Fixed steamdeck's default performance settings.
[*] Fixed tool tips not refreshing sometimes.
[*] Fixed tool tips not displaying the text version of their values (When hovering over the video options menu items is for example)
[*] Fixed issue where main menu fails to load.
[*] Fixed issue when placing nodes on landmasses, they would sometimes go through.
[*] Midi input now should work. In settings, pick your midi device and then click a node to start sending midi to it.
[/list]

[h2]New Free Demo[/h2]
[list]
[*] Has a limited play area.
[*] When loading a saved mix in the demo, you cannot edit it anymore. Can if you purchase the full game.
[*] Character customization is locked
[*] Layer switching is locked
[*] Certain nodes, FX, and instruments are locked
[*] You can place as many nodes as you'd like.
[*] Most tutorials included.
[/list]

[h1]What is next?[/h1]
So now that the event system is in and tutorials are functional, I will be doing a decent bug fixing pass for some of the more jarring known issues. After the bug fixing pass, I can start moving on to a few QoL things for the game.

[h3]2 Next Big things are.[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updating the display of saves so that its much easier to see information about a mix and also make it easier to edit and upload to the workshop. This would also come with the workshop tutorial.
[*] Modulation Update. (The mix playlists is getting moved to after the modulation update since this update will involve a ton of performance optimizations involved with adding FX to mixes).
[/list]

And that wraps things up! 
Please folks, if you haven't already, leave a review for the game as it helps a ton! Also, feel free to join the discord and be apart of the Mixonaut community!

Thank you folks so much for your support and I'm sending happy vibes to all Mixonauts out there!!

notes.title: What does a musical spaceship look like? First Major Update
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=Jlpv1JMWkGA;full][/previewyoutube]

First off, thank you all for playing the game so far and for your patience over the last few months as I figured out “mostly” what the heck was wrong with my body. (I now know I have Meniere's Disease which is the main cause of my vertigo attacks). I’ve got it mostly under control now and have been focused on getting the game stable again.

As stated in previous updates, the full controller support and tutorials exploded into “Oh no.. I’m gonna need to refactor the UI much earlier than expected” which then turned into “Please can I do something else besides UI stuff for a bit” and finally now the game is stable and playable again! So here we go! It’s a lot!

[h2]Tutorials[/h2]

The one thing I still haven’t been able to finish out entirely is the in-game tutorials. I thought I could get them done without having to do the UI refactor yet. What ended up happening was the tutorials became blocked due to the old system being too clunky. Telling the player to select 3D elements and having it find those is a huge pain. **This is now the top priority for January**

[h2]General UI/UX improvements.[/h2]

Here’s an example of the old
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/e51be8ebf08215aaf14155546adc7987af0e28f5.png[/img]

And Now!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/735a77eef91184c646aa0bd0cd140cc52d94f807.png[/img]

[list]
[*] Biggest thing you’ll notice is the icons and just overall look and feel is so much cleaner!
[*] Head-bob is also hidden now in edit mode, but re-appears in flight mode.
[*] Edit mode has a bit of a UI around the edges to make it seem more like a visor display which might be a cool excuse to expand on that later.
[*] Added ability to toggle layer selection during editing and editing voxel landmass nodes.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Mode selection now has images instead of just 1 2 3 4
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/fbef8a17dc4c309ca04bae45655d752480033ee7.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] All 3D UI’s are gone now in favor of a traditional 2D UI. (Some stuff might return in the future like clicking and dragging to change the size of a visualizer node, for now the sliders work just fine)
[*] UI Performance and general editing Performance is much quicker!
[*] Buttons and Sliders got an overhaul with usability and generally are much bigger than before
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/81134259b7f9393bc7c4db54ab8545c95ac47364.png[/img]

[list]
[*] There now is a UI Size Scalar in Settings
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/f9349e6ff1ace08d359dfb73fde8596ddab5b400.png[/img]
[list]
[*] An experimental option for auto focusing on selection can be activated for those who might find it useful for gamepad.
[*] Controller Support is now fully playable. There are still quirks, but UI’s are completely interactable along with editing sliders and clicking and dragging elements.
[/list]

[h2]Notable Bug Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Fixed issue with patterns not being editable after loading
[*] Fixed various issues with the mix skipping during initial playback after load
[/list]

[h2]Why the change from 3D to a traditional 2D UI?[/h2]

Pros of the 3D UI

[list]
[*] They look cool sometimes especially things like knobs
[*] They can feel immersive when editing 2-3 things.
[*] I feel like there is more but can't think of any right now.
[/list]
Cons of the 3D UI

[list]
[*] Nothing in unreal engine is really made nicely for it so everything is custom.
[*] I was building a custom UI on top of an already existing UI system unreal has for 2D
[*] When zoomed out, they essentially turn into 2D anyways
[*] They cost a lot more the render.
[*] Accidental clicks happen way too often
[*] Limited the ability to add features onto nodes since I had to always ask “How is this going to look on the node?” This I should have considered more when playing something like astroneer.. how much work they have to put in to making their 3D UI system look and feel good.
[/list]

Previously.. editing something like this.. would take a ton of CPU resources and time. Here I have around 100 nodes selected all showing me their note values and allowing me to make edits to them! I hope others will see this and feel the same. I do miss the shiny knobs though.

[h2]Multi-Edit is built right in to EVERYTHING[/h2]

In the past, only certain things could be changed across your entire selection.. now, if you edit something, the change will propagate to everything in your selection. The UI will give you an orange dot on anything that is different in your selection. This helps to not accidentally wipe out unique stuff you want to keep while adjusting similar things across the selection.

[h2]Selection filtering and Box Selection[/h2]

In the past, if you selected multiple types of nodes, it would try and pick the last node you selected as the editable node. Now, you get a panel that shows up and are able to click which nodes you’d like to select out of your entire selection. 

Note: There are some quirks to this at the moment which will be ironed out later in regards to things like selecting multiple types of visualizers that have the same editable slider types.

[h2]Note Editor[/h2]

Instead of 2 sliders, there now is a grid that conforms to whatever sample type is used. Drumkits will use a 4x4 grid, Non-scale matched notes will use an 8x12 grid and then scale matched notes will use an 8x7 grid.

In the future, drum kits will also come along with pictures for each of the kit types, but I figured right now it would be good to wait and see if this note editor stays the way it is or not. **The note editor I imagine will constantly fluctuate throughout the length of the project so f**eedback on this is highly appreciated as it will help shape more and more how the note editor works in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/9e5c5999b894fa0db369725504e68fc2ccb4f975.png[/img]

[h2]Patterns and Drums[/h2]

Without the constraint of the 3D UI, patterns and drums can now be a bit easier to parse and edit. This also opens up the idea in the future where pattern and drum visuals aren’t directly tied to how they are edited.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/0eef8c0467719d33ae4e561204319a66e861a43b.png[/img]

Icons and other polish type UI’s will come along with future updates. Things like Vol, Pitch, and Note will be images instead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/44f0f4c91e5d096b840234ef0b432138f7bac0ce.png[/img]

[h2]Categories[/h2]

Create Items and elements are now sorted into categories. Once the categories solidify a bit, I will add images for them.

[h2]Important notes Under the hood[/h2]

So with categories and the UI, setting up the data for everything to route properly means that every single element goes through this system now which is great for adding new things… like.. say new structures and environment types!

[h2]New Structures and Voxel Nodes.[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/dd2f99e073553c35d61b10eaefaa0a7e31efd2a9.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/c6b70a1ed20e52fe4a189cda754d153c0fe20102.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/65cbefb1e4c0446ac51fb47b308c4c1af2281bd0.png[/img]

These are all fairly simple pieces, but you can rotate them and scale them to your hearts content to make quite a few things out of them! (Snapping features is coming later)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/5971b30be0c29cc8e79e66bddde49247b4be760b.png[/img]
Performance-wise, everything is using Unreal 5’s Nanite that can and these pieces are fairly cheap to render. Most of the cost in the game is the volumetric fog, lighting, and shadows (Which can be scaled in graphics settings)

There are also 2 new voxel nodes for you to place which are more cuboid lookin.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/0f6f0654f0cf0ed5d4df2f94b5a4f29876dc1bb8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/e3d4b8d742a00df753fadae6b46dc992ed4a8c6c.png[/img]

These were mostly made to be used to make things like grass spots embedded in the structures, but feel free to go wild!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/0aaa161e4ff5fb680afa1457ebfe5a19a0fd0009.png[/img]

All Structures can spin to the beat now.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/ba40a66241acb2c32b46d8f97fe80578540a31d2.png[/img]
Note: Collision is not changed when doing so to avoid performance issues. This might change in the future when the character can walk on things.

[h2]Voxel Nodes also.. just don’t have limits anymore.[/h2]

The Voxel system used to crash with around 150 nodes… the updated version of it doesn’t crash anymore when exceeding this limit… so uhhh… you are free to melt your GPU enjoy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/5c486bb6df615dad8ce254e43734620857e3010c.png[/img]

Finally, the last thing to talk about is the new environment changes.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/7cbf4c53b3b38413ed1d16cec48337b69e3a181b.png[/img]

This is mostly an excuse to add snow for the winter season in the game. BUT the super nice thing is because of all of the other changes, adding in more content-based things like world types is fairly simple and takes a fraction of the time less to add to the game allowing me to focus more on the visuals and gameplay. 

The default environment now has a cloud layer and a glowing gas giant as the main light. 
This is mostly stuff that the Ultra Dynamic Sky plugin allows to add to it along with a lot of tweaking to parameters to get the Mix Universe look and feel it had before. (I will always battle the purple/blue/pink ratios until the end of time!!) Still might be too blue?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/3fe7531af68f64f96dbcd70e38806c283c967eba.png[/img]

Change World will switch between default and snowy for now until there are more than 2 environments to choose from. These will save into your mix and load into the proper environment later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/f9391cce403c288d0d12544d2ea1e214524d3662.png[/img]

[h2]What’s Next for 2024?![/h2]

So.. take the time estimates with a grain of salt since I am balancing a full-time job along with this.

[list]
[*] Current focus is the in-game Tutorials and a handful of gamepad issues left to sort through. I am hoping that I can get those done by the end of January. (I’ll probably add some more content stuff to play with as well in-between yelling at UI bugs)
[*] Playing Mixes back to back and improved Main Menu and Tutorial Progression
[*] The grid system. Snapping, updating nodes inside of nodes in a much cheaper way. Right now placing a handful of modulators will make layer switching hitch a ton.
[*] Modulation System Finalization and adding 2 more modulator types to play with. These will largely be used to affect the sound.
[*] Input, Keybinds, and In-game UI context (Showing you what buttons to press when you have certain things hovered or selected) Will likely take all of February to do.
[/list]

Not really any order to these yet, but mainly on the list is more content and finalizing ideas and systems I’ve been waiting to finalize for a long time!

[list]
[*] Better workshop interface and main menu integration to show the latest workshop uploads and most popular
[*] Landing on surfaces in flight mode to walk around on.
[*] Character Customization
[*] Midi Export and Import
[*] Generating Environments and Node Setups from scratch.
[*] Exploration mode
[/list]

[h2]New Mixes on the workshop[/h2]

If you want your mix to be noticed, upload it to the workshop and set it to public. Bonus points for joining the discord and posting it in there for others to try out! We’ve got a few folks in there sharing what they make so please feel free to join and share!

A remake by iammattperry of the first part for the song LOST by NF 
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3111181511]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3111181511[/url]

Retrograde orbit by Echo2Omega
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3094737955]https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3094737955[/url]

[h2]And that’s a wrap! Happy New Years and make some cool snowy vibes!![/h2]
Thanks again folks and I look forward to an awesome 2024!

notes.content:
It's almost the end of 2023, but good things are still underway. In the last devlog, I was sure that I could get back to 100% by middle of October and then have something ready by November. 
Long story short, I was wrong and was about 2-3 weeks off, BUT here's the good part!

[h2]I'm back at it 100%[/h2]
The last few months have been super rough for me health-wise so I appreciate the patience! Truly! Everyone who has played the game, given feedback, and left nice reviews I am super appreciative of!

[h2]Controller Support is still the goal![/h2]
Just about everything here is in relation to trying to make the game easier to edit things and ALSO make it nicer for the controller.

What ended up happening instead was that each node had a bunch of 3D buttons that were really hard for the player to juggle. Having things be a bit more traditional in this sense where a UI will show up for each node on the right for editing, not only makes it easier for the player to edit, but also makes it easier for me to add cool new features. notes.title: Devlog: Full Gamepad Support and Unexpected Delays
notes.content:
First of all thank you so much to those who have purchased the game so far!
It's now the end of September and I am still chugging away at gamepad support. I wanted to be as transparent as possible so here it goes.

[h2]I needed a break[/h2]
I had a trip that was planned since the beginning of the year and also just needed a break in general to recharge a bit. I am back now but..

[h2]I also have not been well..[/h2]
I started getting vertigo attacks on a daily basis at the end of August which have basically made it increasingly difficult to make progress. I am still managing to do so, but at a much slower pace. I am hopeful that things will improve here over the coming weeks as I seek more treatment, but I have to be mindful of my health while juggling all the things.

[h2]I underestimated gamepad support[/h2]
Mix Universe is kind of like a weird RTS camera setup when it comes to the user interface. What I ended up landing on was giving the player control of the cursor in edit mode which allows for a lot move flexible UI layouts. You can still hit the D-pad to navigate the main UI's, but the cursor is much more intuitive for things like placing and connecting nodes. Because of this, there were many hurdles that I had to jump through which I wasn't expecting. Something as simple as, how do I tell UI buttons to be selected by fake cursors.. took much longer to figure out than expected. Basically this entire update has become a larger UI undertaking than I imagined.

To give you an idea of what this has grown to be, here's a seemingly neverending list of tasks to make using a gamepad feel nice.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/14f400418d45c5bce04f09c8a11a641c89a0db95.png[/img]

[h2]The good stuff[/h2]
Overall, there are a decent amount of things queuing up for the next update. 
- Almost every UI element will have been updated in some way to try and ease the gameplay a bit.
- I've also gone through and made it so sliders for UI scale actually work properly and the UI automatically scales based on your monitor's DPI. Something like the steamdeck will have big buttons while a 4k monitor will have medium sized buttons. 
- I've also been playing around with auto-focusing selection which can make node editing feel a bit more intuitive out of the gate (You can toggle this in settings)
- 1 2 3 4 buttons have images now.
- Other things like decreasing the amount your camera will freak out if you have hitches and various other bug fixes have come along too.

Here's a bit of what the new UI is starting to look like for the edit menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/79f513e807038ef6e61a9b96c290d89fbb6c4cba.png[/img]

[h2]So when is the next update?[/h2]
I will be shooting for late October and will post another development update if that is to change. I am fairly confident I can deliver a stable update by then. [b]IF you are curious or impatient, you can feel free to check out the experimental beta branch. [/b] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42289276/b99256b0b279d4097e94e4773a3ce2af5a816da2.png[/img]
Please make sure to backup your MixUniverse folder in your documents directory before you do.

As always, thank you so much for being a part of this musical sandbox journey!

Hello Mixonauts! Thank you so much for jumping into Early Access and making cool things! I am so grateful and already am cooking up some really nice improvements to the game.

[*] Fixed a crash related to the my workshop tab.
[*] Added higher resolution mix image taking along with a square and widescreen version. Both of which will be uploaded to the workshop automatically. [*] Fixed issues related to the artist name that should show underneath the mixes name when playing something from the workshop. [*] Changed vibe nodes so that they don't favor 1 timing block nearly as much. Makes for more consistent mixes when playing around quickly.
[*] Fixed cases where modulation elements weren't applying right away during click and drag and double click operations.
[*] Added stats in the profile section of the options menu so you can see how many sounds you've played and how long you've played.
[*] Added some beginner mixes to play around with!
[*] Separated the workshop into My Workshop and My Subscriptions.

notes.title: Mix Universe is out now in Early Access!!
notes.content:
Folks it's time! Early Access for Mix Universe is now LIVE!

This is an incredible moment for me working on the game for the past 5 years. There will be followup videos going over all of the new new things in the build, but first you can take the time to explore for yourself and make some good vibes.

Full Trailer
[previewyoutube=mIGL3UCVQ3I;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mIGL3UCVQ3I[/previewyoutube]

Early Access Launch Fun "How It Started" Video.
[previewyoutube=7m0vGjUkzUQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Big New Things[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Getting Started and Movement in-game tutorials (More to come)
[*] Refactored entire audio FX system to use a new builder system which allows FX to be used as a proper audio FX stack.
[*] There are new landmass voxel nodes to help build out your mix worlds and visualizer nodes.
[*] There are really awesome starter sample mixes and feature mixes included in the game.
[*] An overall pass to just about everything related to visuals has been added. 
[*] Over 100 new instruments are in the game to choose from now. 
[*] Layer Switching is more reliable.
[*] Automatically connect new nodes based on distance when placed.
[/list]

[h2]New Fixes and Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Links have curves now!
[*] Lots of stability updates by fixing various crashes and reducing memory leaks.
[*] Copy paste functionality has been improved dramatically, it will retain node height and pivots based on your cursor position.
[*] You now can preview sounds from the instrument list.
[*] Fixed a lot of issues with note scales and switched minor scales to "Natural Minor" instead of "Melodic Minor"
[*] Added visual indicator for long press buttons.
[*] Options now save properly
[*] Fixed starters activating starters and starters activating starters on patterns.
[*] Fixed cases where links would think they are still connected to previous nodes causing cache corruption.
[*] Removed visual elements for modulation FX for now.
[*] Added visual highlights for selection to make it easier.
[*] Added ability to toggle categories in my mixes panels.
[*] Added category drop down when going to save a mix.
[*] And probably a bunch of other little things I didn't write down.
[/list]

I think it’s important as we go through the Early Access process to be up front about known issues in the game. These are the top 3 critical ones I know about that I’ll be working to try and fix as soon as I can.

[h2]Known Big Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] Sometimes when editing workshop items or saving them, the game can crash. Still investigating a repro case.
[*] When double clicking to populate changes to all selected nodes, a rare crash may occur
[*] There is a known memory leak that gets worse after about 300k sound plays in a session. If you start experience lag after a long play session, restarting the game should fix it. I am working to isolate this issue so I can get a proper solve.
[/list]

There are about 90 known bugs and feature requests that I am chewing through and organizing. However the basic roadmap at this time is to focus on In-Game Tutorials and Bug Fixes for the first month here after launch. Then after, I will have more information on the exact details of what is coming down the pipe. Some really cool stuff for sure!!

Hope you enjoy the game, and feel free to join the discord to leave feedback or share what you make in the game!

notes.content:

Its been about 3 months since the last update and there is a lot going on! I’ll be going to GDC and will be doing 2 talks!

Talk #1 The Tech Behind Bring Music to Mix Universe
[url=https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/technical-artist-summit-mix-universe-the-tech-behind-bringing-music-to-the-universe/891167]https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/technical-artist-summit-mix-universe-the-tech-behind-bringing-music-to-the-universe/891167[/url]

[h2]The Updates![/h2]
[list]
[*] NEW Laser Nodes to add sick laser shows to the mix.

NEW Universal Color Nodes to change hue and brightness during the mix.
Major performance optimizations! So much so that large and complex mixes can run at 30fps now on the steam deck.
Spectrum Visuals are now using Constant Q which results in visual that has a bit more flare to it than default FFT
[*] Upgraded the Quantization System to support much faster speeds without skips. 32nd notes at 200 bpm… is insane.
[*] You can now tell links to use 32nd note timing
[*] Activation Rings on nodes and Radar nodes can be told to go x2 speed making them operate off of 32nd note timing.
[*] Initial controller support and exploration on ways to make controller support better. There is plenty to improve in this category, but its worth mentioning you can do pretty much everything with the controller now navigating menus and 3D UI elements with the D-Pad.
[*] There are now camera modes that allow you to switch from edit mode, to fly mode. Hitting C or clicking the right thumbstick will switch modes. Fly mode is the first iteration of giving Head-Bob more fun ways to navigate mixes.
[*] Mode switching is now set to 1 2 3 4 5 instead of just 1 and 2.
[*] Q and E will now rotate the camera.
[*] You can now rotate the camera and move with WASD at the same time.
[*] ToolTip UI’s will stay open if you quickly mouse past multiple UI’s. This change may not stay the way it is, but its worth trying out.
[*] Slots can now be clicked on to select them before double clicking elements to place
[*] The create menu can now be clicked to create the object and then move the mouse without clicking and dragging.
New Experimental stuff
[*] When flying you can hold down right click or right trigger to send vibes out to nearby vibe nodes. Oh also.. I am experimenting with calling them vibe nodes.
[/list]
[h2]
The Future![/h2]
After GDC, I will be hunkering down to get this into early access! The current goal has been moved from February to mid April. The reasoning behind this is to get more time to improve the new player on-ramp with tutorialization and controller support. Things are busy right now and I am excited to see where it all goes!

notes.title: Heading towards early access Launch in 2023. Playtest Update 3.
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Update 3 for Mix Universe focuses in on multi-editing, randomization, and starting/ending a mix. 

Full Update video here.
[previewyoutube=eDmxAWYPh4g;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What's new and what is fixed?[/h2]
[list]
[*] Patterns are upgraded now to allow them to chain when they aren't set to looping.
[*] Patterns more clearly have start and end points indicated by spherical nodes that you can connect to for activation.
[*] Patterns now have randomization controls to allow for mixes to have much more variety
[*] All Nodes can adjust their height using Q and E which allows for a lot more visual flexibility when laying out mixes.
[*] New Rock Visualizer Node - Similar to the planet node, instead its a rock.
[*] New End Point Node - Stops the mix and shows stats on it.
[*] Every Mix now has an "Origin" layer which you can access in the lower left section of the edit panel. This layer controls which layers 1-6 are activated by default at the start of the mix.
[*] Layer Switchers now show visually which layer they are set to switch to.
[*] Headbob's character model has been updated.
[*] The default space theme's lighting and fog has been updated and particles for the main atmosphere have been fixed.
[*] Multi-Edit double click functionality has been added for Samples, Modulators, Link Duration, Note Duration, Note Octave, and Note Value.
[*] Onscreen UI limit has been increased from 10 to 32 to allow for up to 32 nodes to edit at once.
[*] Simple edit mode has been added which displays a much simpler "Selected" UI.
[*] Added mix history when mixes are uploaded to the store, now if someone is to save a mix off of someone elses mix, we can see where the original mix came from and who made it. 
[*] Added a profile name you can change in the options menu if you don't want to use your steam name for artist info on mixes. 
[*] Added a mix artist overlay which shows title and artist names.
[*] Improved CPU performance when it comes to elements in the scene, still have a ways to go though for much mega mixes. 
[*] Fixed issues with UI's getting stuck during complex edits or longer mix sessions.
[/list]

[h2]IMPORTANT[/h2]
I will be gearing up for an early access launch February 2023. This means that the playtest will be closed to any new players in [b]2 weeks[/b]. December 16th it will not be automatic entry anymore. Request access will still be there, but you might not get access.

[h2]Thank you![/h2]
To everyone involved that has left really useful feedback, offered support, and genuinely wants to see this game succeed I cannot say thanks enough. This game is a continued passion project of mine and I am determined to see it through. There is a still a long and busy road ahead, but I am ready! Best wishes as we head into the holidays and new year!
-Zuko

notes.title: Early Playtest Now Public! Radar Nodes, Better Note Editing and Bug Fixes!
notes.content:
[h1]Early Playtest is now public! [/h1]

Open anyone who requests access! No more needing approval. Discord will also be less locked down than it was now! Thankyou everyone for your support so far!

[url=https://discord.com/invite/VurTMSgqPy]Discord Link[/url]

[h2]Watch this to see the new stuff in action! [/h2]
[previewyoutube=pijNhmaIWtM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]New Stuff[/h2]
[list]
[*] Every node has the ability to add a Synth SAW, SINE, or SQUARE oscilator to it. This is experimental but should be fun to mess with to make sounds more interesting. Combining the piano with a saw wave for instance creates a really neat instrument. 
[*] Updated mixes "Main Menu" and "Radar Starter" to be new update friendly. They can be opened and editing in the "Include" tab under your mixes. 
[*] Added Radar Starter nodes. These nodes will play other nodes when the radar line crosses them.
[*] Added ability to change sizes of modulator rings, visualizer planets, and radar starters by clicking and dragging the rings instead of up and down arrow buttons. Much more intuitive.
[*] Added a duration visual to each node indicated by the length of the glowing spire below them.
[*] Added a closer reverb that has a much tighter falloff. This is right underneath the other reverb element.
[*] Added a much more robust note editing panel above each node. (THIS WILL BE REFINED, I am aware they can be annoying when selecting multiple nodes).
[*] Added ability to set the key per node so that the notes to select are quantized to the closest note value.
[*] Scrolling Up and Down now scrolls up and down when in palettes. Option added to invert this
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed issue with sound only outputing the right and left channels. Middle Channel was dampened quite a bit. This may cause previous mixes to sound too loud.
[*] Decreased time needed to register a double click so its easier.
[*] tool tip for values stays around when modifying values now.
[*] octaves now visually start from 1 instead of 0
[*] When Changing graphics settings, everything should restore properly now. Keeping the warning text for a little bit longer until that is 100% confirmed.
[*] Fixed crash that was seemingly random related to multi-band compressor. It was my fault.. i told the audio components to destroy themselves on accident. 
[*] Fixed issue with links not displaying the timing elements properly when connecting to bigger nodes. 
[/list]

[h2]Performance[/h2]
[list]
[*] There is still a chance you will have issues on lower end hardware. CPU Usage may be high but GPU usage will likely be cut in half cost-wise! Super stoked about this one. 
[/list]

[h2]Known Annoying Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] There is a pretty awkward selection bug that can happen when you switch modes sometimes. Nodes will seemingly be not selected but will show their element panels as if they are selected. Still continuing to figure out a repro case for it.
[*] Slots for elements can float around randomly during editing. Seems to go away after deselection.
[*] Higher end frequencies don't seem to be respecting the volume controls as much as they should. This could make tweaking drums a bit difficult. 
[*] Tempo UI slider is visually broken. Works ok functionally though.
[/list]
